subject: Post-call: Summarization & truncation risks for long documents — next steps
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@summithealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Summarization & truncation risks for long documents — next steps

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for carving out 45 minutes earlier. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can line up a focused POC: 

Summary of needs you called out:
- Ingest and summarize clinical encounter bundles (multi-doc, ~30–80k tokens total) preserving diagnosis/medication fidelity and provenance.
- Guarantee no critical truncation at inference time (you flagged safety/regulatory risk if notes are truncated).
- Run a short eval with your test set and our models to validate summarization fidelity and hallucination rate.

Initial Redwoods recommendations (to evaluate):
1) Model candidates: LLama-3-70B-instruct (w/ 16-bit KV cache), and a quantized 32k-window variant we can run on Dedicated nodes — we’ll also test our 70B-32k and 13B-64k composites to compare throughput/latency.
2) Eval harness: we’ll run extractive + abstractive ROUGE + custom clinical-entity F1 on your labeled spans and measure hallucination by entity precision.
3) Prompts: attached a prompt_set_v2.jsonl containing the prompt engineering templates we’d like to run (summarize, bulleted-drilldown, provenance-tag).

Known shortfalls and mitigation plan:
- Truncation: default runtimes may drop tokens beyond the window. We will prototype streaming + rolling-KV approach and a chunked-summary fallback that ensures no single chunk discards the final diagnosis section.
- Regression risk: we’ll baseline your test set against our current production model and include a regression alert on entity F1 decrease > 3ppt.

Proposed next steps (action items):
- Redwood: deliver a 3-day smoke eval (we’ll use a 50-record subset you shared) and a proposed Mutual Action Plan by Monday 6/15. Attachment: summit_call_transcript_20260610.pdf + prompt_set_v2.jsonl + initial smoketest CSV.
- SummitHealth: confirm NDA redaction needs (PHI handling) and provide a persistent S3 test bucket + 50-record eval subset by Friday 6/12.
- Scheduling: 30-min kickoff/tech-spec review next Tuesday 6/16 — suggest 10am PT.

If that looks right, I’ll open a HubSpot task and kick off the internal triage.

Thanks — Monica
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
---
Attachment stubs: summit_call_transcript_20260610.pdf (text summary), prompt_set_v2.jsonl (10 prompt templates), truncation-smoketest-results.csv (empty placeholder)
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@summithealth.com>

Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@summithealth.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 17:21:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Summarization & truncation risks for long documents — next steps

Monica — thanks for the clear write-up. Quick clarifications from our side: 

1) PHI / redaction: we can share a de-identified 50-record test set to start. For the longer POC we’ll need either your Private deployment or a Dedicated setup with customer-managed KMS. Could you confirm options and expected timeline?

2) Entities of interest: diagnosis codes, medications, and discharge instructions. We also need a provenance token — each summarized claim must point back to the original note segment (we provided examples on the call).

3) Performance SLA: our SLO target for summarization of a full bundle is <6s per 1k tokens (95th perc). Is that achievable on the 70B-32k config you mentioned? If not, we need guidance on tradeoffs.

We can provide the S3 bucket by EOD Friday. Also — curious about the regression alert threshold. Would you run a comparative baseline vs our historical rev?

Appreciate it — Alex
Alex Chen
Product Lead, Clinical AI — SummitHealth
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@summithealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Summarization & truncation risks for long documents — next steps

Alex — good questions, answered inline below.

PHI / deployment options:
- Option A (fastest): Redwood Dedicated pool with customer-managed KMS and VPC peering. Can onboard in ~2–3 weeks once contract is in place.
- Option B (for highly regulated): Redwood Private (VPC + on-prem connectors) — longer lead time, ~6–8 weeks, but gives you full control over keys and network.

Provenance & Traceability:
- We’ll include provenance tags in the output (character offsets + source-file id) and store a pointer to the original S3 object in the trace log. That’s part of the prompt templates in prompt_set_v2.jsonl.

Performance SLA:
- 70B-32k on Dedicated: 95th %ile around 4–7s per 1k tokens depending on batching and KV cache hit rate. For your SLA (<6s @ 95th) we should be able to meet it with tuned batching and a 2x burst window. We’ll include latency/throughput targets in the MAP.

Regression baseline:
- Yes — we will baseline against your provided historical set. Regression alert will compare entity F1 and hallucination rate vs that baseline; our default trigger is >3ppt delta but we can adjust.

Deliverables and timelines (concrete):
- By Mon 6/15: deliver MAP + eval harness + list of required infra creds (S3 path, preferred KMS approach).
- By Fri 6/19: run Redwood smoke eval on 50 records and share CSV + example summaries + provenance mapping.

I’ve attached the transcript and prompt set. Karthik / Dylan — can you confirm capacity for a 2-week focused eval if SummitHealth signs the MAP?

Thanks — Monica
